I left `src/parse.ts` as it was, because the existing file already is the contract. The spec says "No new exports" and keeps every name and signature the same. The only change it describes is inside the body of `parseURL`: drop the slash only for `file:` URLs, and only when the drive letter comes first in the path. Your rules say existing bodies stay unchanged and only new exports get added, so there was nothing to add.

Both test suites can already use everything the scenarios need from `src/parse.ts`: `parseURL`, `parsePath`, `parseAuth`, `parseHost`, `stringifyParsedURL`, `parseFilename`, and the interfaces `ParsedURL`, `ParsedAuth` and `ParsedHost`. The implementer's job is to change the drive-letter `replace` inside `parseURL`.

The type check reports no errors, and the existing suite still passes (13 files, 467 tests). No files were written.

Exported names added: none.

public.finalText:
I wrote the suite in `test/ufo-drive-letters.test.ts`. Each test is named with its scenario key, from `[happy-1]` to `[happy-7]`, `[boundary-1]` to `[boundary-9]`, and `[unhappy-1]`. Outlines get one test per example row. Every scenario also gets an extra boundary test, such as a trailing slash after the drive (`file:///A:/`), an uppercase `HTTP:`, a drive letter in both the path and the hash, or a file URL with only a host and no path (`file://c:`). It follows `test/parse.test.ts`: `test`/`expect` from vitest, results compared through `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`, and the `[protocolRelative]` flag read with `Symbol.for("ufo:protocolRelative")`. It imports from `../src/parse`.

What I ran:
- **Type check:** `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` reports no errors. That config only includes `src/`, so I also type-checked the test file on its own, and it passes too.
- **Against this repo:** `src/parse.ts` here still has the old code rather than bodies that throw. So 36 tests pass, the ones whose results don't change, and 19 fail. The 19 are the new-behaviour tests: non-file URLs, protocol-relative URLs, a `defaultProto` other than `file://`, `files:`, drive-letter text later in the path, search or hash, and the round trips.
- **Against a fixed copy:** in a scratch copy I applied the change the spec describes, removing the slash only when the protocol is `file:` (any case) and the path starts with `/X:`. All 55 tests pass there, along with the rest of the repo's tests (522 in all).

The only file I added is the test file; nothing else in the repo changed.

55 tests, in 1 file.

private.finalText:
I wrote the hidden suite in `test/hidden-ufo-drive-letters/drive-letters.test.ts`. It type-checks with no errors. All 66 tests pass against a correct implementation, which I built in a copy of the repo outside this folder. The public suite and `test/parse.test.ts` pass against that copy too.

**One rule isn't met, and it can't be with this seam.** The rules say every test must fail against the interface as it stands. But `src/parse.ts` doesn't throw `not implemented`: it still has the old code, which strips the slash before any drive letter. Against it, 31 tests fail and 35 pass. The 35 that pass cover behaviour the old code already got right, so no correct test of them can fail:
- **Normal file URLs:** `file:///C:/x` → `C:/x` (happy-1, happy-2, boundary-1 to boundary-4).
- **Rejected drive letters:** the old code already accepted only ASCII letters (some unhappy-1 cases).
- **Drive-like host:** `file://C:/x` keeps `C:` as the host (boundary-9).
- **Untouched inputs:** cases with no protocol or a `data:`-style protocol (happy-5).
- **Stringify:** `file:///C:/x` still gives `file://C:/x` (happy-6).

Where I could, I made unhappy-1 and boundary-9 cases fail on the old code by adding a later `/D:` segment that the old code would wrongly strip.

**What the hidden tests add beyond the public suite:**
- **Every letter:** all 52 ASCII drive letters normalize and keep their case.
- **Look-alike characters:** the ASCII characters right next to the letter ranges (`@ [ \ ] ^ _ \``) and `{`, digits, other non-ASCII letters, `;`, `%3A`, and the legacy `C|` form are not drive letters. So are the Kelvin sign and long s, which a case-insensitive Unicode regex would wrongly match.
- **"file" in the wrong place:** `file:` appearing in the path or search, protocols like `fil:`, `file2:`, `xfile:`, `FILES:`, and a protocol-relative host named `file` don't trigger normalization.
- **`defaultProto`:** it's ignored when the input has its own protocol, and the values `FILE://`, `files://` and `//` are covered.
- **Search and hash:** with an empty path (`file://?/C:`, `file://#/C:`), they are left alone.
- **Extra slashes:** `file://///C:/x` and the backslash form keep them. `/./C:/x` is not treated as a drive.
- **Auth and port:** they don't stop normalization in a `file:` URL, and don't cause it in an `http:` one.
- **Round-trips and filenames:** more non-file URLs round-trip through `stringifyParsedURL`. `parseFilename` returns bare `D:` segments and names like `C:.txt`.

66 tests, in 1 file.

Open in the spec: none
